title: Sleep-related Alzheimer’s disease vulnerability in aging: A muscle-metabolic perspective
title_zh: 老化中与睡眠相关的阿尔茨海默病易感性：肌肉代谢视角
abstract: Sleep disruption is a hallmark of aging and a plausible driver of Alzheimer's disease vulnerability. Reduced slow-wave sleep, increased fragmentation, and circadian instability may facilitate amyloid-β accumulation, tau propagation, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and impaired glymphatic clearance. Yet the physiological factors that predispose older adults to unstable sleep remain insufficiently integrated into models of brain aging. This Review advances a sleep-muscle-brain framework in which sarcopenia, sarcopenic obesity, and insulin resistance are conceptualized as modifiable muscle-metabolic conditions that may bias sleep continuity and shape the biological impact of sleep disruption. We examine irisin/FNDC5-BDNF signaling as a hypothesis-generating candidate modifier of metabolic regulation, neurotrophic support, and brain resilience, while emphasizing that direct evidence for a causal role in human sleep regulation remains insufficient. Irisin-related pathways intersect with insulin sensitivity, inflammatory control, and BDNF-dependent synaptic plasticity, all of which are relevant to the physiological context in which sleep disruption may influence Alzheimer's disease pathophysiology. We propose that age-related attenuation of muscle endocrine signaling, together with insulin resistance and low-grade inflammation, may lower the threshold at which sleep fragmentation translates into amyloid/tau dyshomeostasis, glial activation, and network dysfunction. Rather than treating sleep disturbance as an isolated brain-centered risk factor, this framework positions sleep as a biobehavioral hub through which peripheral aging processes can modulate neurodegenerative resilience. The Review integrates evidence from sleep neuroscience, geroscience, metabolism, and neurodegeneration, and identifies experimentally testable predictions. A sleep-muscle-brain perspective may help refine risk stratification and guide multimodal interventions combining sleep optimization, resistance exercise, metabolic targeting, and Alzheimer's disease biomarker monitoring.
abstract_zh: 睡眠紊乱是老化的典型特征，也是阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer’s disease）易感性的潜在驱动因素。慢波睡眠减少、睡眠碎片化增加和昼夜节律不稳定可促使Aβ沉积、tau传播、神经炎症、氧化应激和糖淋巴系统清除受损。尽管如此，促使老年人睡眠不稳定的生理因素仍未被充分整合进脑老化模型。本文提出睡眠—肌肉—大脑框架，将肌少症（sarcopenia）、肌少症性肥胖（sarcopenic obesity）和胰岛素抵抗视为可调节的肌肉代谢状态，这些状态可能偏倚睡眠连续性并塑造睡眠紊乱的生物学影响。我们讨论了irisin/FNDC5-BDNF信号通路作为代谢调节、神经营养支持与脑韧性修饰的候选机制；并强调其在人体睡眠调控中的直接因果证据尚不足。irisin相关通路与胰岛素敏感性、炎症调控及BDNF依赖的突触可塑性相交叉，这些都与睡眠紊乱影响阿尔茨海默病发病机制的生理背景相关。我们提出，年龄相关的肌源性内分泌信号减弱，联合胰岛素抵抗和低度炎症，可能降低了睡眠碎片化转化为淀粉样蛋白/τ失衡、胶质激活与网络功能障碍的阈值。该框架认为睡眠不仅是孤立的脑中心化风险因素，而是一个生物—行为枢纽，通过该枢纽外周老化过程调制神经退行性韧性。该综述整合了睡眠神经科学、老年学、代谢学与神经退行的证据，并提出可检验的实验预测。睡眠—肌肉—大脑视角有望优化风险分层，并指导将睡眠优化、阻力训练、代谢干预与阿尔茨海默病生物标志物监测相结合的多模态干预。
